scoring.selector: m2b_score.select: the delivered final answer less the host's search-limit notice (optimus.agent.index_turn.LIMIT_NOTICE); its digest is the script's
scoring.hardening: Fable CP1 finding 2: ordinary-word symbol names count only as code (backticks, a call) or by qualified name; numbers match whole; fences cut at the cap count; QO4's unfenced code-like lines must be the file's own; QB1 F2 drops hedge phrases; a path echo plus a hedge fails every case but QO4 (tested)
scoring.v3: Codex finding 5: claim-bound citations (path and code-form symbol in one clause, or a range of at most 40 lines overlapping the symbol); loci; fact groups; runner status first (stop reason or output at the cap: INCOMPLETE); boundary rows; the QO4 quote control needs the exact contiguous block
scoring.v4: Codex attempt 2 finding 5: a fact is a relationship, every group and its supporting locus in one paragraph, no carrying sentence negated unless the fact is a negation, forbidden extras absent; loci name code or a forward narrow range; reversed ranges fail; an answer is scored only on a settled row; a boundary needs the declared stop, zero requests and no emitted answer; the QO4 control needs exactly one exact fenced block and no other code, or a sentence naming the requested lines or source as unavailable with no code. Tested with independently written answers and contradictions, including Codex's QB2 example
scoring.v5: Codex attempt 3 finding 5 (lexical matching cannot establish what a claim asserts): the deterministic checks are a screen. A screen FAIL or INCOMPLETE is final; a screen PASS is PENDING_AUDIT and becomes PASS only by a recorded support-audit ruling `supported` (FAIL when `unsupported`). Forbidden phrases catch the literal reversals Codex listed (QB2 lexical-first, QB3 excluding framing, QR2 unset, QO1 discard/skip, QO3 ignore/truncate). A boundary needs a clean expected_zero_call row on the runner's own allowance (so F on QO1/QO2 before the outline is a boundary), the declared stop, zero requests and no emitted answer. The QO4 control needs one closed exact block with only line endings normalized, or a non-negated sentence naming the requested lines as unavailable with no code
scoring.v6: Codex attempt 4 finding 5: an audit record carries `identity` (release, case, arm, the delivered answer's SHA-256, snapshot, scorer and cases digests; m2b_score.audit_identity) and `rulings`, one per CP3 reviewer (two, distinct), each a boolean `supported` with a non-empty reason. A screen PASS is PASS only when the identity matches exactly and both rulings are supported, FAIL when both are unsupported; missing, mismatched, incomplete or disputed rulings stay PENDING_AUDIT (a dispute is held for the operator) and contribute to no gate. QO4: each configured refusal phrase is an assertion (`not available` included); the rest of its sentence may not negate or deny it; inline code beyond a bare name or path is purported source and fails, as do code-like unfenced lines. QB3's forbidden phrases name only the framing reversal

runner.guard: Codex findings 3 (round 122, attempts 2-3): the Guard refuses before forwarding unless the row's allowance (at most one send per row, enforced by run_one), the released model (the approved hash fixes its route), the approved hash and output cap, the input cap (the route's estimator), every earlier send reconciled, and the ceiling's reservation counting those earlier sends' unsettled attempts all hold; each refusal is recorded, and the host's own record of a refused request is kept apart (unforwarded_receipt_ids), never charged
runner.accounting: each send records at dispatch the host request identity the runner gives its receipts (`receipt_base`, `<run>:answer:1:<dispatch>` for Q's one-request Chat turn); a receipt matches a Gateway attempt only under that identity with the attempt's ordinal, Gateway id and disposition (a completed attempt the host records as uncertain keeps both, its charge unknown), and any route request id or attempt number its usage names must agree. Attempts come only from Gateway evidence: each physical Gateway attempt is one attempt; a send the Gateway reported nothing for is MAX_ROUTE_ATTEMPTS unknown attempts once, its host records kept beside them and never counted again. Identical matched copies are one charge; differing copies leave it unknown. A receipt matching no attempt is kept and flagged; each distinct receipt identity not already settled is charged once as money only (an unattributed charge creates no attempt), conflicting copies flagged. Any failure of the run keeps its row and receipts and stops the run
runner.terminal: expected_zero_call only with the case's declared stop reason and no emitted answer: the delivered text is exactly production's too-large notice for a required file (workspace_context.blocking_from_diagnostics); otherwise incomplete
